questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I have the hundred reasons to not attend the meeting tomorrow.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
I have the hundred reasons to not attend the meeting tomorrow.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the unnecessary use of the article "the" before the term "hundred reasons."
  • Articles like "the" are used for specific items, and in this case, it is not needed.
  • The correct phrase should be "I have a hundred reasons," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
  • Thus, the error is located in part 1 of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: "I have a hundred reasons to not attend the meeting tomorrow."
 
Note: This is a PYP question, and the official answer key has marked (correct option) as the correct answer, hence we cannot make any changes to it.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. Sheila ______ (failed) all her classes.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets to fill in the blank.
Sheila ______ (failed) all her classes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. passed.

Key Points

  • The word "failed" means to be unsuccessful in achieving one's goal, especially in the context of examinations or assignments. (असफल होना)
    • Example: She failed to meet the deadline for the project submission.
  • "Passed" means to be successful in an examination or course. (उत्तीर्ण होना)
    • Example: Sheila passed all her classes with flying colors.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'failed' is 'passed'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. passed.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Flunked (असफल होना): To fail in a course or examination.
    • Example: He flunked the math test last semester.
  • Resized (पुनः आकार देना): To change the size of something.
    • Example: She resized the image to fit the new layout.
  • Flopped (विफल होना): To fail completely, especially in a performance or business.
    • Example: The movie flopped at the box office.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. After I retire, I started a second career as a writer and published several books which allowed me to share my stories and insights with a wider audience.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
After I retire, I started a second career as a writer and published several books which allowed me to share my stories and insights with a wider audience.

options.text: and insights with a wider audience
options.html: and insights with a wider audience

options.text: After I retire, I started a second career
options.html: After I retire, I started a second career

options.html: as a writer and published several books

options.text: which allowed me to share my stories
options.html: which allowed me to share my stories

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of tenses.
  • The phrase "After I retire, I started" is incorrect because "retire" is in the present tense and "started" is in the past tense.
  • The correct phrase should be "After I retired, I started," ensuring grammatical correctness and consistency in tense usage.
  • Thus, the error is located in part 2 of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
Correct Sentence: "After I retired, I started a second career as a writer and published several books which allowed me to share my stories and insights with a wider audience."

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The children have made the box.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The children have made the box.

options.text: The box is being made by the children.
options.html: The box is being made by the children.

options.text: The box had been made by the children.
options.html: The box had been made by the children.

options.text: The box has been made by the children.
options.html: The box has been made by the children.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "The children have made the box."
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the box" at the beginning.
  • Change the active verb form "have made" to "has been made" (present perfect passive).
  • Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the children."
  • Ensure that the new sentence makes sense and retains the original meaning.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Correct Sentence: "The box has been made by the children."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "The box is being made by the children." – This is present continuous passive, not present perfect passive.
  • Option 2: "Children had made the box." – This is not in passive voice; it's past perfect active.
  • Option 3: "The box had been made by the children." – This is past perfect passive, not present perfect passive.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. A. The upper part of the river B. Continuous rain on C. Week, there had been D. During the previous
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
A. The upper part of the river
B. Continuous rain on
C. Week, there had been
D. During the previous
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (2) i.e. DCBA
Key Points
  • The sentence begins with the time reference "During the previous," which is correctly indicated by part (D). 
  • Following the time reference, "week, there had been" (DC) continues the logical sequence, establishing the timeframe.
  • The next part, "Continuous rain on," starts explaining the situation, indicated by (B).
  • Ending with "The upper part of the river" (A) completes the sentence by stating the affected area.
Therefore, the correct answer is DCBA.
Additional Information
  • Option 1 (DBAC): This option starts with "During the previous continuous rain on," which disrupts the logical sequence and makes the sentence awkward.
  • Option 3 (ADCB): This option starts with "The upper part of the river during the previous," which places the subject before the timeframe, leading to confusion.
  • Option 4 (ABCD): This option starts with "The upper part of the river continuous rain on," which makes the sentence grammatically incorrect and illogical.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. They are organizing a concert for charity.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
They are organizing a concert for charity.

options.text: A concert is being organized by them for charity.
options.html: A concert is being organized by them for charity.

options.text: They are organizing a charity concert.
options.html: They are organizing a charity concert.

options.text: They are being organized a concert for charity.
options.html: They are being organized a concert for charity.

options.text: A concert for charity is organizing by them.
options.html: A concert for charity is organizing by them.

questions.solution: The correct answer is: Option 1. The conversion is from Active to Passive voice. Explanation: The Active voice in this sentence is in Present Continuous tense (Subject + is/are + V4 + Object). Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Continuous tense (Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + is/are + being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case)). Here, "They" (Subject in Active) becomes "by them," and "a concert for charity" (Object in Active) becomes the Subject in Passive.

questions.question: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence. A. When we connect this design with a wire, electricity flows. B. These metal strips were put in a sulphuric acid solution. C. He made two strips of different metals. D. Alessandro Volta discovered electric battery.
questions.questionHtml:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence.

A. When we connect this design with a wire, electricity flows.
B. These metal strips were put in a sulphuric acid solution.
C. He made two strips of different metals.
D. Alessandro Volta discovered electric battery.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • The paragraph begins by introducing the discovery of the electric battery by Alessandro Volta.
  • Sentence D is the first sentence as it introduces the main subject:
    • "Alessandro Volta discovered electric battery."
  • Sentence C follows as it describes the initial steps Volta took in his experiment:
    • "He made two strips of different metals."
  • Sentence B is the third sentence because it explains what was done with the metal strips:
    • "These metal strips were put in a sulphuric acid solution."
  • Sentence A is the fourth as it describes the outcome of the experiment:
    • "When we connect this design with a wire, electricity flows."
  • The correct sequence is DCBA.
 
Coherent paragraph after rearrangement:
"Alessandro Volta discovered electric battery. He made two strips of different metals. These metal strips were put in a sulphuric acid solution. When we connect this design with a wire, electricity flows."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
